en: 4. The Question on the Diversity of Kamma.
"Venerable Nāgasena, for what reason are not all humans equal? Why is it that some have short lives while others have long lives;
some are afflicted with many ailments while others are free from illness; some are ugly while others are beautiful; and some have little influence?"
“Some have great influence, some have little wealth, some have great wealth, some are of low birth,
some are of noble birth, some are lacking in wisdom, and some possess wisdom? The Elder replied:
“But why, Great King, are not all trees the same—some sour, some salty, some bitter, some pungent, some astringent, and some sweet?
“I think, venerable sir, it is because of the difference in their seeds.
“In the very same way, Great King, because of the difference in their kamma, humans are not all the same; some have short lifespans...”
Some have long lives, others have many ailments; some have few ailments, others are ugly, while others are beautiful;
some have little influence, others have great influence; some have little wealth, others have great wealth; some are born into low families, others are born into high families;
some are lacking in wisdom, while others possess wisdom.
“Great King, this was also said by the Blessed One:

‘Young man, beings are owners of their actions, heirs of their actions, born of their actions, bound by their actions, and have their actions as their refuge; it is action that divides beings, namely, according to their inferiority or superiority.
The fourth question: On the Differentiation of Kamma.
